fact.text: The salmon parasite Paramoeba perurans is itself a host: another single-celled organism lives permanently inside it, like a lodger in a lodger.

heads_up: Šiandien Vilniuje – Kariuomenės dienos eitynės, praskris naikintuvai.
Šiandien Belgijos oro uostai uždaryti 8–22 val. dėl streiko, skrydžiai atšaukiami.

lithuania.headline: Nalšios šiaurinėje apygardoje Seimo nare išrinkta liberalė Mėta Paulauskė
lithuania.summary: Antrajame ture liberalė Mėta Paulauskė surinko 50,53 proc. balsų ir vos 82 balsais aplenkė valstietį Gintautą Kindurį; rinkėjų aktyvumas siekė 27,89 proc., o galutinius rezultatus VRK tvirtins lapkričio 27 d.
lithuania.context: Pirmalaikiai rinkimai surengti, nes gegužės pabaigoje mirė šioje apygardoje 2024 m. išrinktas liberalas, kanojininkas Jevgenijus Šuklinas. Pirmajame ture varžėsi 11 kandidatų, į antrąjį pateko Paulauskė ir Kindurys.

lithuania.headline: Mokytojų streikas: mokiniai palaiko, bet nerimauja dėl egzaminų
lithuania.summary: Mokytojams streikuojant dėl didesnių atlyginimų ir geresnių darbo sąlygų, Moksleivių sąjungos prezidentas Martynas Dikšaitis sako, kad dauguma mokinių juos palaiko, bet abiturientai ir vienuoliktokai nerimauja dėl pasiruošimo egzaminams ir praleistų pamokų atidirbimo.
lithuania.context: Mokytojų profesinės sąjungos ilgai reikalavo didesnių atlyginimų ir geresnių darbo sąlygų. Nesulaukę sprendimų, mokytojai pradėjo streiką, o mokyklose kol kas vyksta tik užimtumą užtikrinanti veikla.

lithuania.headline: Biudžeto ginčas: „pinigų nėra“, ieškoma naujų pajamų
lithuania.summary: Seimui svarstant kitų metų biudžetą, koalicijoje nuskambėjo kaltinimų, kad projektas „suklastotas“, o Barysas teigia, kad priėjus ribą „pinigų nėra“; finansų ministras Taurimas Valys neatmeta PVM mokėtojo ribos didinimo, svarstomas ir automobilių taršos mokestis.
lithuania.context: Lietuva pastaraisiais metais smarkiai didino gynybos išlaidas, todėl biudžete atsirado skylė. Valdančioji koalicija ieško, kaip ją užlopyti, o kiekvienas naujas mokestis kelia ginčų tarp partnerių.

world.headline: COP31 climate talks collapse without a deal
world.summary: The longest UN climate summit ever ended in Turkey without its main deal after the EU, UK, Pacific islands and others rejected a text that never mentioned fossil fuels, while poorer countries objected to the lack of clear finance; it is the first such collapse since Copenhagen in 2009.
world.why: Covered by 9 outlets, top of BBC and Google News
world.context: UN climate summits have been held yearly since 1995; the 2015 Paris Agreement set the goal of limiting warming to 1.5–2°C. COP28 in 2023 first called for 'transitioning away' from fossil fuels, and how far to go beyond that has split countries ever since.

world.headline: Democrats win largest US House majority since 1992
world.summary: Chuck Hubbard unseated Republican Virginia Foxx in North Carolina by 330 votes after a recount, giving Democrats at least 258 House seats to the Republicans' 173, with four races still open; Democrats also won the Senate.
world.why: Covered by 7 outlets, #1 on Google News
world.context: The midterm elections earlier this month were the first national test of Donald Trump's second term, which began in January 2025. Rising living costs during the war with Iran were a top issue, and Democrats won seats even in deeply Republican states such as Alaska, Texas and Iowa.

world.headline: AI bubble fears hit markets; South Korea's KOSPI falls up to 5.8%
world.summary: Asian markets slid on Monday after Friday's rout, when the S&P 500 fell 3.7% into a correction and the Nasdaq lost 5.3%, wiping out its 2026 gains; US futures point to a rebound, and Trump blamed the slide on Democrats' midterm wins.
world.context: Since ChatGPT's launch in late 2022, AI-linked companies such as Nvidia have driven much of the global stock market's gains, and worries that valuations have run ahead of profits have grown.

world.headline: At least 24 killed in Indonesian candy factory fire
world.summary: A fire at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia candy factory in Cikande, about 50 km west of Jakarta, killed at least 24 people, and rescuers are searching for about 30 still missing; an air-conditioner short circuit is the suspected cause.

interesting.headline: Alcaraz beats world No. 1 Zverev for first ATP Finals title
interesting.summary: Carlos Alcaraz beat Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 (9-7) in Turin for his 14th straight win, becoming the youngest of only four men to win all four majors and the ATP Finals.
interesting.context: Alcaraz was out for four months with a wrist injury and returned only at the US Open in August.

interesting.headline: BepiColombo becomes second spacecraft ever to orbit Mercury
interesting.summary: The European-Japanese probe entered orbit around Mercury, though a glitch was reported.
interesting.context: BepiColombo launched in 2018; only NASA's Messenger had orbited Mercury before.

interesting.headline: South Korea's education minister quits over AI exam cheating scandal
interesting.summary: Choi Kyo-jin resigned after last-minute measures against AI cheating, including three nationwide emergency phone alerts on exam day, caused chaos at the college entrance exam; 111 candidates were caught with devices.
interesting.context: The scare began when the top scorer in a tax accountancy exam admitted photographing questions with a microcamera and getting answers from AI.

interesting.headline: Elizabeth Holmes doc 'You Can See Everything' passes $100m
interesting.summary: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's A24 documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes has passed $100 million worldwide and is the first documentary watched by 1 million Letterboxd users, with a 4.61 average rating.
interesting.context: Holmes founded blood-testing start-up Theranos and was convicted of fraud in 2022.

ongoing.title: Russia-Ukraine war
ongoing.update: A Russian strike on an apartment block in Dymer near Kyiv killed 11, and a 7-year-old boy was pulled alive after 14 hours in the rubble; a Russian warship docked in Libya's Benghazi sank after a suspected Ukrainian drone attack, and Poland confirmed three Russian cruise missiles fell on its territory on Friday.
ongoing.context: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 after annexing Crimea in 2014. Kyiv repelled the attack on the capital, and the war became a grinding front-line fight in the east and south, with long-range drone and missile strikes on both sides. US-led peace efforts have so far failed to end it.

ongoing.title: US-Iran tensions
ongoing.update: Oil tankers were set ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran unveiled a dual-missile launcher and warned that enemies are trying to stir unrest, and truck drivers went on strike across Iran over economic hardship.
ongoing.context: Tensions over Iran's nuclear programme turned into open conflict when Israel and the US struck Iran in 2025. This year the fighting widened into a war around the Gulf, with a US blockade, attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and strikes on energy facilities.

ongoing.title: Protests across France and Europe
ongoing.update: Belgium's national strike against €10bn of austerity cuts shuts the country's airports on Monday, as air traffic control halts service from 7am to 9pm local time; it is the 11th strike to hit Belgian airspace in 11 months.
ongoing.context: Protests over living costs and public services began in France this autumn and have taken place every weekend since. Young people and unions elsewhere in Europe, from Spain and Portugal to Belgium, have joined with their own demands against cuts.

ongoing.title: Israeli operation in the West Bank
ongoing.update: Dozens of settlers set fire to homes and about a dozen vehicles in at least four Palestinian villages near Ramallah, which opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, now trying to form a government, called 'Jewish terrorism'.
ongoing.context: Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. After the Hamas attack of October 2023 and the Gaza war, Israeli raids and settler violence in the West Bank sharply increased.

ongoing.title: Sudan civil war
ongoing.update: Drone strikes on Khartoum damaged homes and a UN building, and an army source said the drones were launched from Ethiopia.
ongoing.context: Sudan's war began in April 2023 when the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces turned on each other in a power struggle. It has killed tens of thousands and created the world's largest displacement crisis.

ongoing.title: Saudi Arabia-Houthi fighting
ongoing.update: Yemen's Houthis claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh oil refinery and the coalition intercepted a ballistic missile; Saudi officials say Houthi attacks have killed 26 people in the kingdom since September.
ongoing.context: The Iran-backed Houthis seized Yemen's capital in 2014, and a Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015. A truce from 2022 largely held until fighting resumed amid this year's wider regional war with Iran.

ongoing.title: Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy
ongoing.update: The New York Times reported that Alice Huang was in touch with a Chinese spy agency during the affair, and the US intelligence chief said top Nvidia chips have 'ended up in places that they should not'.
ongoing.context: Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO on 12 November after reports of affairs, including with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, which allegedly facilitated about $12bn of chip sales in breach of US export controls. Lawmakers now ask how China got around those controls.
